Kenya_2026-10-11_weekly_precip: ECMWF S2S ensemble-mean rainfall for 11 to 18 October is heaviest in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N (about 100 mm) and over the northeast toward the Ethiopian and Somali borders (40 to 70 mm), while central and southern Kenya stay below 10 mm. From 18 October to 8 November the rain spreads into the southwest and the central highlands with 30 to 50 mm per week, and 70 to 95 mm at the western edge of the domain over Lake Victoria. The north remains mostly below 20 mm per week through 22 November.
Kenya_2026-10-11_gefs_weekly_precip: GEFS keeps most of Kenya nearly dry for 11 to 18 October, with rainfall confined to the west near the Uganda border around 1N (locally 60 to 100 mm) and a band above 100 mm north of 5N in southern Ethiopia. The wettest week is 25 October to 1 November, with 60 to 90 mm across western and central Kenya along the equator and 70 to 90 mm in the northeast toward the Ethiopian border. From 1 to 15 November 30 to 60 mm persist over the southwest and central highlands, and the northwest stays below 15 mm throughout.
Kenya_2026-10-11_weekly_precip_downscale: Downscaled ECMWF rainfall for 11 to 18 October exceeds 100 mm in the west near the Uganda border, along the eastern border and the north coast, and in the far north across the Ethiopian border, while the central interior and the south stay below 10 mm. From 18 October onward the maximum shifts to the central highlands just east of 37E near the equator, where weekly totals exceed 120 mm in the weeks of 18 to 25 October and 1 to 8 November. The week of 1 to 8 November is the wettest overall, with additional maxima of 90 to 120 mm in the southwest and near the southern border around 3S, and the northwest remains dry in every week.
Kenya_2026-10-11_weekly_medium_range_pre: The medium-range ECMWF forecast for 11 to 18 October puts 60 to 90 mm along the eastern border and north coast, across the northeast and north of 4N, and along the western border, with the interior from the northwest down to the southern border mostly below 15 mm. For 18 to 25 October the rain shifts south, with 60 to 90 mm in a band from Lake Victoria across the central highlands between the equator and 2S and 30 to 50 mm over the east and the coast. The northwest is the driest area in both weeks at 10 to 20 mm or less.
Kenya_2026-10-11_chance_of_above_or_belo: The tercile balance for 11 to 18 October leans strongly above normal (+75 to +100 points) over the east, northeast and coast, the west near the Uganda border and the central highlands on the equator, against a below-normal lean of -50 to -90 points in the far southwest across the Tanzanian border. For 18 to 25 October the north flips to below normal (-30 to -75 points north of 3N), while the area south of 1.5N stays above normal at +50 to +100 points, peaking in central Kenya near the equator. From 25 October to 22 November a moderate above-normal lean of +25 to +75 points persists over the south and southwest, with little signal in the north.
Kenya_2026-10-11_efi_sot_precip: A wet extreme is signalled for 11 to 18 October in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N, where the EFI reaches 0.8 to 0.9 and is enclosed by SOT contours of 0 and 1, and along the eastern border with Somalia and the northeast, where the EFI is 0.6 to 0.8 with positive SOT. For 18 to 25 October a weaker signal (EFI 0.55 to 0.7, SOT above 0) sits over central Kenya between the equator and 3S near 37.5E. Only isolated cells just above 0.5 remain for 25 October to 1 November in the south, and there is no wet-extreme signal from 1 November onward.
Kenya_2026-10-11_50th_percentile_exedanc: The chance of exceeding the model-climate median for 11 to 18 October is 90 to 100% over the eastern half and northeast, the west near 1.5N and the central highlands on the equator, but only 1 to 25% in the far southwest across the Tanzanian border. For 18 to 25 October the north drops to 10 to 45% north of 3N, while probabilities south of 1.5N are 75 to 99% and peak above 99% in central Kenya on the equator. From 25 October to 22 November most of the country sits at 55 to 90%, with 90 to 99% along and south of the southern border up to 8 November.
Kenya_2026-10-11_anomaly_from_50th: The ensemble mean for 11 to 18 October is about 80 mm above the model-climate median in the west on the Uganda border near 1.5N and 30 to 60 mm above it along the eastern border and the coast, with near-zero anomalies in the centre and slightly negative values in the far southwest. For 18 to 25 October the largest positive anomaly (+30 to +50 mm) is over central Kenya on the equator, while the area north of 3N is slightly drier than the median (-5 to -15 mm). From 25 October to 22 November anomalies of +10 to +40 mm persist over the south and southwest, largest across the Tanzanian border, and the north stays near zero.
